Stickman tiers: style and concept fixes, before and after

Six Myth vs Reality beats rendered through the locked tier pipeline: render, QA (text verdict from OCR), Real-ESRGAN 2× upscale to 1920×1080, then the programmatic text overlay where the tier needs it. “Before” images are the Phase 4a bake-off renders of the same beats.

QA judge calibration

Default: gpt-4o-mini, detail high, on a 768 px downscale. Its OCR is accurate: a text verdict computed in code from the transcription agrees with my labels on 93% of the 45 images it judged. Its own pass/fail calls agree far less (27%). Claude Haiku 4.5 agreed 90% on text but returned malformed output on 24 of 45 images and costs more ($0.0035 vs $0.0022 per image). Neither judge reached 80% on style (69% and 48%), so style, cast and concept are advisory: logged and used to rank best-of-2 candidates, never used to block an image.

Before and after

Beat 7

Concept recipe: SYMBOLIC0:26 · ‘This is the image burned into your head.’

Handwritten recipe concept for this check: The viewer with a big white thought bubble above his head containing one horned helmet.

Before, every model drew a stickman wearing a helmet. Now the viewer has a thought bubble containing the helmet, on both tiers.

Beat 69

Concept recipe: ESTABLISHING4:37 · ‘In 1876, composer Richard Wagner's opera cycle’

Handwritten recipe concept for this check: A grand opera house facade at night with a lit marquee over its doors and a few tiny stick figures at the entrance.

The opera house facade is now the subject. V3 renders “BAYREUTH, 1876” itself (OCR-checked); V2 leaves the marquee blank and the text is overlaid in code.

Beat 125

Concept recipe: POV8:29 · ‘Next time you see those curving’

Handwritten recipe concept for this check: The viewer's hands in the foreground holding a lunchbox, a horned cartoon mascot on a stadium banner in the middle distance.

Before, both models produced confusing close-ups. Now the viewer’s hands hold a lunchbox in the foreground, with a horned mascot on a stadium banner in the middle distance.

Beat 117

Style fix7:57 · ‘Wagner's costume department gave you a myth’

Arms and legs are thin stick lines now, not trousers and boots. The ‘labeled MYTH’ phrase was stripped in this per-beat compile, so both tiers correctly render no text.

Beat 10

Style fix + text0:38 · ‘So did any Viking ever actually strap on horns’

The viewer’s legs are stick lines on both tiers. V3 spells the question right; V2 (FLUX) gets it from the overlay, so no more ‘Vickings’.
